title: Oliver's band stranded in Baltimore, then Milwaukee with Elgar
summary: The band got stranded in Baltimore, Bigard ate hot dogs and then cabbage for days, then Omer Simeon wrote Charlie Elgar and Bigard spent months in Milwaukee before Luis Russell sent for him in New York.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When you recorded with King Oliver after you had joined Duke, in '27 and in '28, --
-- who was on the sides that you made? Who -- you said King Oliver didn't have a band then. Who was on the recording session?
That was his band. You see, his band was stranded --

-- from Chicago. You see, we was on the road and we got stranded and when I left there Omer Simeon was the first lead alto and we got stranded in Baltimore. And, finally, the guy gave a dance, and we didn't have any money or

nothing. I ate hot dogs for three days straight. And we were staying in this rooming house, this lodging. The woman began to cook cabbage and hot dogs, and I never ate cabbage in my life. I didn't like it. But then when I began to get hungry after three days of hot dogs, I ate An everything. I ate the cabbage and everything she had on that table and it started me to eat cabbage. And that's when the band broke up.

And, finally, Simeon wrote to a man named Charlie Elgar in Milwaukee and Charlie sent for Simeon and Simeon said, "I'm going to try to get you to come to Milwaukee." So when he went to Milwaukee -- and Charlie Elgar was from New Orleans, too, but I didn't know him -- and Simeon told him about me and so he sent for me. That's when I worked in Milwaukee about four, five months.
And that would have been what year?
Oh, that would have been in about '24 or '25.

Then I left. Luis Russell, he went to New York and he had a gig and he told me to come to New York, he's got a job for me. I tried to get Simeon to come, too. He didn't want to leave. And that's how I got to New York.
